src/manual/content

Authored product manual pages. Frontmatter supplies stable document IDs, titles, grouping and order; all Markdown files in this tree enter the served corpus.

Parent folder

<!-- directory-inventory:start -->

Files and subfolders

Each entry links to the file or to the child folder's guide. Source summaries are navigation aids; they do not replace the implementation or its tests.

File or folder Responsibility
architecture/ Architecture manual pages explaining ownership, execution flow, persistence, integration contracts and contributor workflows.
legacy/ Historical manuals retained in a separate navigation category. These explain prior implementations and must not be read as current setup instructions.
01-home.md smTO Manual: smTO uses the model to interpret requests and choose tools, with durable execution and actual result receipts.
02-install-startup.md Install and startup: This guide installs SMTO from source code, meaning the original project files rather than a ready-made installer. You need Python 3.11 or newer, a copy of the project supplied by the maintainer, and an AI model that works with SMTO. These steps use a terminal, an app for entering commands. You may need help from someone with technical experience.
09-configuration-storage.md Explain shared Settings saves, separately revisioned startup overrides, saved conversation/task retention policies, expiry protection and observed countdowns, alongside storage and removable-destination controls. Link detailed persistence, recovery and UI flows to their implementation guides.
16-parameter-store-context-sql.md Use saved parameters, exact accepted references and Database connections. Explain successful-binding approval, explicit correction and interrupted Apply recovery, ordered learned workflows, accepted snapshots and provider-specific authentication behavior.
18-integration-execution-api.md Integration execution API: Use this API when another program needs to submit an Agent request and read a JSON result. It delegates to the same Controller request and continuation services used by the product. Normal access, accepted terms, tool selection and execution policy still apply. The API does not create a separate executor or permission bypass.
19-ui-pages-tour.md Tour Agent pages, task interactions, diagnostics, loaded-content search and retained conversation views. Explain accepted deletion versus cleanup, saved assistant context, Directory route metadata and tab-session navigation alongside owning workflow guides.
21-gmail-integration.md Gmail Integration: smTO is not an email client. Gmail is the source of truth. smTO does not maintain a mailbox copy, inbox index, message/thread cache, draft mirror, label cache, or background synchronization database. Searches and reads query Gmail when requested.
22-schedules.md Scheduler Manager: These are smTO reminders and future Agent actions. Live Google Calendar appointments, invitations and availability use the separate Google Calendar skill. Creating or deleting an item in either domain never changes the other.
23-notifications.md Notification Center: Open Notifications from the bell in the Agent header, Directory, or the Schedules navigation. /notifications brings together scheduled reminders, scheduled Agent outcomes, monitor alerts, durable task updates and system notices.
24-proxmox.md Using Proxmox VE: The Proxmox skill manages virtual machines and containers through your selected Gateway. It is disabled by default, including upgrades of older capability selections. Enable/add proxmox in the applicable prompt, conversation or global capability selection when you need it. A parameter reference cannot enable it or grant permission to change a server.
25-model-configuration.md Model configuration and routing: Assign Main and optional Helper in Inference or Settings → Model routing. Each role can use a different provider, model, context ceiling, API key and generation profile. Additional installed models and managed instance profiles remain available for later assignment.
26-auth-and-email.md Authentication and outbound Email: Email / SMTP is enabled by default; an explicit saved capability selection or exclusion still applies. Enable Authentication to use its standalone administration tools. Configuration lives in Parameter Store. Templates are detached prefills: opening a template does not save a profile, connect an account or send a message.
26-errors-diagnostics.md Interpret stable Error IDs and occurrence evidence, use the diagnostic Console and distinguish retained answers from verified completion. Explain heartbeat freshness, local GPU readings, stack prerequisites and scoped Agent Check recovery without treating observations as execution receipts.
27-google-workspace.md Shared Google Workspace identity: One Google Workspace Account in Parameter Store can authorize Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive. Its google_account record owns the private access/refresh tokens, verified Google subject and email, expiry and granted scopes. There is no second credential database.
28-google-calendar.md Google Calendar: The google_calendar skill reads and changes live Google Calendar data. Google owns the calendars, appointments, invitations, recurrence and availability. There is no local calendar mirror and no synchronization into smTO schedules.
29-google-drive.md Google Drive: The google_drive skill works with live My Drive and Shared Drive data. It creates no local Drive mirror or search database. Enable Google Drive in Capability Policy and reuse the shared Google Workspace account in Parameter Store. No scope is requested when the skill is installed or discovered.
30-microsoft365.md Microsoft 365: The microsoft365 skill operates live Outlook mail, calendars, personal contacts, OneDrive and authorized SharePoint libraries through Microsoft Graph v1.0. Enable Microsoft 365 in the existing Capability Policy. Installing it does not change saved capability snapshots or request consent.
31-slack.md Slack: The slack skill performs live workspace operations. Enable Slack in the existing Skills capability policy. Slack owns messages, conversations and files. The skill has no workspace mirror, index, crawler, background listener or helper model. The main Agent interprets requests and summarizes the bounded results.
32-github.md GitHub: Enable the optional GitHub skill in capability selection, then create a GitHub Account in the Parameter Store editor. Prefer a fine-grained PAT restricted to the exact repositories and permissions needed. Enter its GitHub login, numeric account ID, token, explicit authorized_repositories (owner/repo names), and granted_permissions.
33-office.md Office documents: The office skill inspects, creates and edits Word DOCX, Excel XLSX and PowerPoint PPTX files on the selected Gateway. It uses the existing capability selection and permission policy. Document contents are untrusted data: text in a file never grants authority or becomes an instruction.
34-pdf.md PDF documents: Enable the optional pdf skill to inspect and transform PDFs on the selected Gateway. It makes no helper model calls. Document text, field values, metadata and OCR results are untrusted data; they cannot authorize actions or supply instructions.
35-docker.md Docker and Compose: Enable the optional Docker skill to inspect and manage the Docker Engine on the selected Gateway. It provides 56 typed tools. Logs, image metadata, labels and Compose output are untrusted data; they cannot authorize an action. Backend operations make no helper model calls.
44-workflow-recorder.md Workflows — saved requests: A Workflow saves an exact prompt and selected execution settings. Run now starts a fresh Agent task, including normal model reasoning and tool use. Each run has its own conversation and history. Identical inputs do not guarantee identical output.
45-inference.md Inference management: The Inference area manages vLLM and llama.cpp from the controller. Open /inference from desktop or mobile navigation, or from the surface directory. It uses your existing sign-in, appearance settings and agent permission policies.
46-themes-backgrounds.md Themes and conversation backgrounds: Open Settings → UI Preferences → Edit themes, colors and conversation background, or visit /theme. Desktop and mobile Appearance controls open the same editor. These choices belong to your browser; they do not change the Agent's behavior.
47-policy-editors.md Editing permissions and capabilities: Permissions control whether an otherwise permitted operation runs, asks for approval or is denied. Capabilities control the Skills and tools available to the Agent and how automatic selection chooses them. Enabling a capability does not supply credentials or approve its operations.
48-artifacts-downloads.md Generated files and previews: Open Artifacts from this run on a task to find its generated files. Image cards can also appear in the answer; other files have preview and download controls. The run center remains available when a run has no files or its files were deleted. Use its category filter to browse images, data, documents, interactive files, archives and other content.
49-attachments-vision.md Attachments, archives and Vision: An attached file has an exact context_id, recorded name, media type, size and digest. The task receives a bounded metadata manifest with a suggested reader. This makes the file discoverable without automatically reading every page or sending every image to a model.
50-monitors.md Monitors and condition triggers: A monitor checks command output on one Gateway for a condition. It records observations and can create a notification and an Agent action when the condition matches. Use Schedules for work that should happen at a future time.
docs-skill.md Docs skill: The Docs skill lets the Agent search the same Manual you can browse. It runs locally on the controller and is read-only. It needs no Gateway, network, credentials or running Manual web service. A fresh installation makes Docs eligible for automatic capability selection. You can explicitly exclude it; saved explicit selections are preserved when upgrading.
memory-editor.md Memory Editor: Open Settings → Agent behavior → Memories → Open Memory Editor, or choose Memory Editor in Directory. Direct links use /memory-editor?key=memory.key.
prompt-editor.md Prompt Editor: Open Settings → Agent behavior → Prompts → Open Prompt Editor, or choose Prompt Editor in Directory. Direct links use /prompt-editor?key=prompt.identifier.
